convertibility_reason: Uses iCustom for Laguerre indicator which is not a built-in MT5 indicator. The rest uses built-in iCCI and iMA, but the custom indicator dependency requires manual handling or pre-computation of Laguerre values.

derived_values.name: MA current bar vs MA previous bar comparison for trend direction
derived_values.formula: ma0 > ma1 (MA at Shift vs MA at Shift+1)

long.left: Laguerre == 0 AND MA(0) > MA(1) AND CCI < -CCILevel

short.left: Laguerre == 1 AND MA(0) < MA(1) AND CCI > CCILevel

other_exits: Virtual SL/TP: position closed on tick when price moves SL/TP points beyond open price; Signal-based close: Laguerre>0.9 closes buy, Laguerre<0.1 closes sell

position_sizing.conditional_logic: If Lots>0 use fixed Lots; if Lots==0 use deposit fraction: FreeMargin*MaximumRisk/1000; if DecreaseFactor>0 reduce lot after consecutive losses by aLots-aLots*losses/DecreaseFactor

custom_logic_notes: Virtual SL/TP mechanism: when VirtualSLTP=true, no SL/TP orders are sent to broker; instead OnTick checks if current price has exceeded SL or TP levels from open price and closes position programmatically. Entry also blocks if CloseBuy or CloseSell signal is active simultaneously with Open signal (OpenBuy && !OpenSell && !CloseBuy). Deviation for order execution is set to Spread*3. Lot normalization rounds to volume step and clamps to min/max volume. SL/TP validation checks against broker StopsLevel before placing real SL/TP orders.
python_conversion_notes: The Laguerre custom indicator must be reimplemented in Python (gamma-based FIR filter with 4 coefficients). Virtual SL/TP requires tick-level monitoring since positions are closed programmatically on each tick. The DecreaseFactor lot reduction logic iterates deal history backward counting consecutive losses - this must be replicated against backtest trade history. The MA comparison uses current bar (Shift) vs previous bar (Shift+1) for momentum direction. Entry gate checks no existing position on the symbol (single position per symbol). The deviation=Spread*3 should map to a slippage tolerance in Python backtesting.
